messages.content: 你能幫我找到紐約有閱讀室和小說區的公共圖書館，然後在洛杉磯有Wi-Fi和有兒童區的公共圖書館，最後在芝加哥有咖啡廳和閱讀室的公共圖書館嗎？

function.name: public_library_find_nearby
function.description: Locate nearby public libraries based on specific criteria like English fiction availability and Wi-Fi. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Boston, MA

We need to pass an array of facilities? The type says facilities: "Wi-Fi" | "Reading Room" | "Fiction" | "Children Section" | "Cafe"[]. That seems ambiguous: maybe facilities can be one of those strings or an array of strings? The example says "Cafe"[] meaning array of Cafe? Actually "Cafe"[] means array of "Cafe"? So facilities can be a string or an array of strings? The type is union of string or array of string? But the function expects a single argument object with location and facilities. The facilities field can be a string or an array of strings. For multiple facilities, we should pass an array of strings. So for each city:

NYC: reading room and fiction. So facilities: ["Reading Room", "Fiction"].

LA: Wi-Fi and children section. So facilities: ["Wi-Fi", "Children Section"].

Chicago: cafe and reading room. So facilities: ["Cafe", "Reading Room"].

We need to call the function three times. The function returns any. We need to output the results. We'll call the function for each city.
